reasons: The research summary, assumptions and log counts are fixed text, so the page can show results that were never calculated for the company.
The assumption fields and Update button do not change the model, and the page says a recalculation will be added later.
The Excel export claims formulas but writes only values.
Server text is placed into the page as HTML without escaping, which is a risk if the model returns unexpected markup.
No automated tests or error handling for missing fields were found in this file.

used_by: No caller is visible in this file. It is probably served by the backend as the main page.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Page setup and colour theme
sections.what: Loads the fonts and the chart and Excel libraries, then sets the page colours and the fixed top bar. The colours are kept in one place so the whole page can be restyled from here.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping colours in one place lets the look change without editing each element.
sections.watch_out: The page needs internet access to load these libraries, so charts and export stop working offline.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Header, two-column layout and timeline line
sections.what: Styles the logo, the export button, and the two-column layout with a main flow on the left and an activity panel on the right. A thin glowing line runs down the left side to link the steps.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The layout uses fixed heights based on the header size, so changing the header height means changing these values too.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Step cards and company name box
sections.what: Styles each numbered step with a glowing dot on the timeline, and styles the company name box with an orange glow when it is selected.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Buttons, cards and assumption rows
sections.what: Styles the main orange button, its hover and disabled looks, the content cards, and the rows used to show each assumption.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The disabled style is the only signal that a build is running, so it matters for the user.

sections.name: File setup (part 5)
sections.title: Assumption inputs, chart area and tables
sections.what: Styles the small number boxes used for assumptions, the Update button, the fixed-height chart area, and the financial tables.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Charts are given a fixed height, so they will not resize to fit their content.

sections.name: File setup (part 6)
sections.title: Agent panel and hiding helper
sections.what: Styles the table row highlight, the right-hand activity panel, its entries, and the rule that hides any element with the hidden class.
sections.why: Likely reason: the hidden rule uses a strong override so that other styles cannot keep an element visible.
sections.watch_out: Hiding and showing steps depends on the hidden rule, so removing it would show every step at once.

sections.name: File setup (part 7)
sections.title: Loading spinner and tab styles
sections.what: Styles the spinning loader shown during a build and the three tabs for the financial statements, including which tab is active.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: File setup (part 8)
sections.title: Small-screen layout and the first two steps
sections.what: Changes the layout to a single column on narrow screens. Then the page markup for the header, the export button (hidden at first) and steps 1 and 2 is added.
sections.why: Likely reason: the export button starts hidden so that it only appears after a model exists.
sections.watch_out: The export button is shown only by the build code, so it stays hidden if the build path changes.

sections.name: File setup (part 9)
sections.title: Steps 3 to 5 and the start of the script
sections.what: Adds the markup for the assumptions step, the three-tab statements step, and the charts and valuation step. Then the script begins with the state object that stores the company, the model, the assumptions and the active tab.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: File setup (part 10)
sections.title: Starting the model build
sections.what: When the user clicks Build or presses Enter, this sends the company name to the quick-model endpoint. On success it keeps the reply and shows steps 2 to 5 and the export button. On failure it shows an alert and restores the button.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The build assumes the reply contains a list of steps and the summary sections. If any of these are missing, the page shows an error after part of the results may already be drawn.

sections.name: File setup (part 11)
sections.title: Assumptions and research summary
sections.what: Returns a fixed set of assumptions (starting revenue, growth rates, margins, tax, cost of capital) and writes a fixed research summary into step 2. The summary names a fixed industry and model along with the company name.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: These values are typed in, not read from the server. The page can show them as if they came from the research, so they must not be treated as results.

sections.name: File setup (part 12)
sections.title: Assumption inputs and statement section setup
sections.what: Builds the assumption boxes for starting revenue, first-year growth, gross margin and research cost, each with an Update button. Then the statement section starts by reading the revenue figures from the reply.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The number boxes are not connected to the model, so changing them has no effect on the results.

sections.name: File setup (part 13)
sections.title: Income statement and cash flow tables
sections.what: Builds the income statement table (revenue, gross profit, EBITDA and net income) and the cash flow table (free cash flow), each showing five years in millions of dollars. The balance sheet tab only shows a message saying it is not built yet.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The table headers always say Year 1 to Year 5, so a model with a different number of years would be shown incorrectly.

sections.name: File setup (part 14)
sections.title: Revenue line chart
sections.what: Draws a line chart of revenue over five years, in millions, using the page's orange and grey colours.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The chart uses the same five labels as the tables, so it depends on there being exactly five years.

sections.name: File setup (part 15)
sections.title: Cash flow chart and valuation cards
sections.what: Draws a bar chart of free cash flow and then shows three valuation figures: enterprise value, WACC and terminal value. The Update action for recalculation only shows a message that it is not built yet.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The recalculate function is a placeholder, so the page cannot yet update results from changed inputs.

sections.name: File setup (part 16)
sections.title: Tabs, Excel export and activity log
sections.what: Switches between the three statement tabs. Export builds an Excel file with three sheets (income statement, cash flow and valuation) and downloads it. The activity log function adds a labelled entry to the right-hand panel.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The export writes the numbers only. The activity log says it includes formulas, which is not true, so a user checking the file will not find working formulas.

sections.name: File setup (part 17)
sections.title: Enter key starts the build
sections.what: Listens for the Enter key in the company name box and runs the build. This gives the same result as clicking the button.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The Enter key is not blocked while a build is running, so a quick second press can send a second request.

summary: This is the main ORACLE web page. It takes a company name, asks the server to build a simple three-statement financial model for it, and shows the income statement, cash flow, a revenue chart and a valuation, with an Excel export.
purpose: It is the front end of the financial model builder. The user types a company name and sees the results on one page, while a side panel shows what the agents did.
why: Likely reason: one plain page with no build step keeps the front end simple while the server does the modeling. The file also has placeholders, which suggests it is an early version that is still being built.
how: First, the page loads its styles and the Chart.js and Excel libraries. When the user clicks Build Financial Model or presses Enter, the page calls the quick-model endpoint on the server. It saves the reply in a state object. Then it fills the research section with fixed text, the assumptions section with fixed numbers, the income and cash flow tables, two charts, and the valuation cards. Export to Excel writes three sheets from the saved reply. Switching tabs only changes which table is visible.
inputs: The company name typed in the text box. The reply from the server, which must include the all_steps list, the income statement summary, the cash flow summary and the valuation summary. The numbers in the assumptions boxes are shown but not used.
outputs: Visible sections on the page: research summary, assumption boxes, income and cash flow tables, two line and bar charts, valuation cards, and an activity log. An Excel file named after the company is downloaded when Export is clicked.
risks: Several values on screen are fixed text or fixed numbers, not results. The industry (Technology / Software), business model (SaaS), comparable count, and 'Performed 5 web searches' and '45 calculation steps' messages are typed in, so they may not match the company. The Update button in the assumptions section only shows an alert. The Excel export says it includes formulas but writes plain numbers. Server text is placed into the page as HTML without escaping. The Enter key can start a build while the button is disabled.
debug: If the page shows an alert saying the build failed, check the reply from the quick-model endpoint in the browser's network tab. If charts are missing, check that the Chart.js library loaded from its CDN. If Export does nothing, check that the xlsx library loaded. If numbers look wrong, compare them with the reply, since every money value is divided by one million for display. If the research text does not match the company, that is expected, because it is fixed text. The activity log keeps growing across builds because a reset is not run between them.
